ok.noise: Understandable, but the room is loud
ok.level: Understandable, but your volume needs fixing
ok.tone: Understandable, but your voice sounds a bit off
ok.none: Understandable, with a few small issues

hard.noise: Hard to follow: the room is too loud
hard.level: Hard to follow: your volume is way off
hard.tone: Hard to follow: your voice doesn't sound like you
hard.none: Hard to follow: several small things add up

score.overprocessed: Too much processing: it's cutting your voice

explain.clear: Your voice comes through clearly, and the room stays out of the way.
explain.good: You sound good. A couple of small changes will make it even better.

ok.noise: People can follow you, but the background noise competes with your voice.
ok.level: People can follow you, but they'll need to adjust their volume.
ok.tone: People can follow you, but your voice doesn't sound quite natural.
ok.none: People can follow you. A few small things add up, so fix them one at a time.

hard.noise: The background noise is almost as loud as your voice, so words get lost.
hard.level: Your volume is far off, so listeners will struggle or hear crackles.
hard.tone: Your voice is far from natural, so words are harder to make out.
hard.none: Many small problems add up. Start with the first tip.

explain.overprocessed: Noise removal or the gate is so strong that it chops your words and changes how you sound.

explain.tonal: You can clearly hear a fan or machine.
explain.hum: A low electrical hum is audible.
explain.broadband: A steady hiss or room noise is audible.
explain.cutToSilence: Your pauses are cut to total silence, which chops the start and end of your words.

explain.good: Your voice sits at a comfortable level.
explain.tooQuiet: Listeners will have to turn you up, and that turns the room up too.
explain.tooLoud: You're close to the limit, so loud moments can crack.
explain.distorting: Your loudest moments hit the limit and crackle.

explain.boomy: Too much bass, so words blur together.
explain.boxy: A boxy, cardboard sound covers your words.
explain.hollow: Your voice sounds hollow and far away.
explain.muffled: Your voice sounds muffled, like talking through a cloth.
explain.harsh: The upper tones are pushed, so it can sound sharp and tiring.
explain.sharpS: S sounds come out sharp and hissy.
explain.dull: There's little sparkle on top, so consonants sound dull.
explain.thin: There's not much bass, so your voice sounds thin.

placement.cardioid: Point the back of the mic at the loudest noise, like a fan or computer
placement.supercardioid: Keep the loudest noise off to the side of the mic, a little behind it
placement.other: Move the mic closer to you and further from the noise

action.moveCloser: Move closer: about one fist away ({{cm}} cm)
action.fans: Switch off fans or machines you can while recording
action.noiseReduction: Turn on noise reduction with our ready-made settings
action.gainUp: Turn the input volume (gain) up a little
action.gainDown: Turn the input volume (gain) down a little
action.backOff: Back off a little — bass builds up when you're very close

speakInto.end: Speak straight into the top of the mic
speakInto.side: Speak straight into the front of the mic, where the logo usually is

action.angleMic: Angle the mic slightly off to the side of your mouth
action.usbPort: Plug your audio interface into a different USB port (back of the computer)
action.compWet: Raise the compressor's Wet by about {{db}} dB
action.eqByEar: Try the gentle by-ear tweak in our ready-made EQ settings

gain.meaning: How much the mic's signal is turned up before anything else happens.
gain.analogy: Like the volume knob on a guitar amp: more makes you louder, and the room too.

noise.meaning: Any sound that isn't your voice, like fans, hiss, traffic or hum.
noise.analogy: Like the chatter at the next table in a café.

snr.meaning: How much louder your voice is than the room.
snr.analogy: Like talking in a quiet library versus a busy train station.

db.meaning: The unit for how much louder one sound is than another.
db.analogy: Like steps on a staircase: every 10 dB up sounds about twice as loud.

eq.meaning: Turns parts of your voice up or down, from deep bass to bright top.
eq.analogy: Like the bass and treble knobs on a stereo.

noiseReduction.meaning: Learns what the room sounds like while you're quiet, then takes it out of your voice.
noiseReduction.analogy: Like noise-cancelling headphones, but for your mic.

compressor.meaning: Evens out your volume by gently turning down the loud parts.
compressor.analogy: Like a friend who turns the TV down whenever an ad blasts.

gate.meaning: Lowers the mic when you stop talking, so your pauses stay quiet.
gate.analogy: Like a door that opens when you speak and closes when you stop.

sibilance.meaning: The hiss in S, SH and T sounds.
sibilance.analogy: Like a snake's hiss when there's too much of it.

proximityEffect.meaning: The extra bass you get when you're very close to the mic.
proximityEffect.analogy: Like a radio host's deep voice when they lean right into the mic.

cardioid.meaning: A mic that hears mostly from the front and very little from the back.
cardioid.analogy: Like a flashlight that lights up what's in front of it, not behind.

confirmed.nasal: You hear your voice as nasal, and we measured it too: the middle tones sit above your target. The EQ settings include a cut for it.
confirmed.muffled: You hear your voice as muffled, and we measured it too: the low-middle tones are thick or the clear upper tones are weak.
confirmed.boomy: You hear your voice as boomy, and we measured it too: there is more bass than your target.
confirmed.thin: You hear your voice as thin, and we measured it too: there is less bass than your target.
confirmed.harsh: You hear your voice as harsh, and we measured it too: the upper tones sit above your target.
confirmed.sharpS: You hear sharp S sounds, and we measured them too.
confirmed.dull: You hear your voice as dull, and we measured it too: there is less sparkle on top than your target.

byEar.nasal: You hear your voice as nasal. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.muffled: You hear your voice as muffled. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.boomy: You hear your voice as boomy. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.thin: You hear your voice as thin. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.harsh: You hear your voice as harsh. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.sharpS: You hear sharp S sounds. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.
byEar.dull: You hear your voice as dull. We didn't measure this, but you hear it — here's a gentle tweak in the EQ settings.

refine.wrongDistance: This take was recorded at {{actual}}, but the settings were made for {{dist}}, so it can't tell whether they work. Record again at {{dist}}, or get new settings made for {{actual}}.
refine.gateTooHigh: The gate was closing on your voice: its Threshold goes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
refine.gateDoubled: ReaGate's Dry is at {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB with Wet open, so your voice goes through it twice and gets about 6 dB louder whenever the gate opens. Dry goes to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

chopped.reafirHalf: Noise removal is cutting your voice: lower the ReaFIR reduction to about half of what you set.
chopped.toAi: ReaFIR keeps cutting your voice: turn it off and use AI noise removal instead (Elgato Noise Removal).
chopped.gateOff: The gate still cuts your voice: switch ReaGate off in Wave Link (or turn its Wet all the way down and set Dry to 0 dB).
chopped.aiLower: The noise remover is cutting your voice and your pauses: lower its strength, or try Voice Focus in Wave Link instead. Pauses should sound quiet, not dead silent.
chopped.other: Something in Wave Link is cutting your sound to total silence. Switch your effects off one at a time to find which one does it.

refine.tooLoud: Your voice is too loud and hits the limit, so it distorts: the compressor's Wet goes down {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
refine.tooLoudGain: Your voice is too loud and hits the limit, but the compressor's Wet is already at 0 dB: turn your mic gain down in Wave Link (or on your interface) until loud words stay under the limit.
refine.quieter: Your voice dropped {{drop, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, so the compressor's Wet goes up {{db, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB, to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

thin.boom: Your voice lost bass: the 150 Hz low shelf goes from {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
thin.warmth: Your voice lost warmth: the 250 Hz band goes from {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

harsh.presence: Your voice got harsh: the 3.5 kHz band goes from {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.
harsh.top: Your voice got harsh: the 10 kHz high shelf goes from {{from, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB to {{to, number(maximumFractionDigits: 1)}} dB.

refine.harshFromClipping: Your voice sounds harsh because it is too loud and distorts, not because of the EQ. Fix the loudness first; the EQ stays as it is.

stillNoisy.reafirMore: The room is still almost as loud as before: drag the ReaFIR curve down about 3 dB more, then listen.
stillNoisy.toAi: ReaFIR isn't removing enough of the room: switch to AI noise removal (Elgato Noise Removal).
stillNoisy.addAi: The room is still almost as loud as before: add AI noise removal (Elgato Noise Removal) at the top of your effects.
stillNoisy.aiStronger: The room is still almost as loud as before: turn your AI noise removal up one step.

changeApproach.ai: Changing numbers isn't helping. Use AI noise removal (Elgato Noise Removal or NVIDIA Broadcast) instead of ReaFIR.
changeApproach.placement: Point the mic at your mouth and away from fans, the PC and windows.
changeApproach.closer: Move closer to the mic: the closer you are, the less of the room it hears.
